judgment.rationale: The issue remains reproducible on the latest stable release, but the existing archive was collected after PowerToys restarted. PR #50273 has now merged the required Runner session-end instrumentation, so the next useful evidence is a fresh preview-build report captured immediately after the next exit.
evidence: The issue reports that the PowerToys tray icon and tools disappear after several hours while Command Palette remains active.
On 2026-09-04, the reporter confirmed that the behavior happened again after upgrading to the newest stable release from GitHub.
The reporter explained that the attached PowerToys report was generated only after restarting PowerToys.
Maintainer moooyo stated on 2026-08-31 that the supplied log contained no distinguishing failure evidence and that more logging was needed.
PR #50273 merged on 2026-09-07 and adds Runner logging for WM_QUERYENDSESSION and WM_ENDSESSION without changing session-end behavior.
Issues #50270, #49438, and #49208 contain similar public reports of PowerToys disappearing while Command Palette or other utilities remain unavailable.
judgment.recommended_action: Wait for a preview containing PR #50273, then request a fresh diagnostic archive immediately after the next Runner disappearance.

fix_assessment.rationale: Merged PR #50273 directly covers the current investigation by recording Windows session-end and Restart Manager close-app signals. It improves observability rather than correcting a confirmed root cause.

issue_context.summary: PowerToys' tray-hosted functionality reportedly exits after hours of normal desktop use while Command Palette stays active. The behavior now reportedly persists on a newer stable build, but the only submitted diagnostic archive was collected after a restart and cannot identify why the Runner exited.
known_information: The original report used PowerToys 0.100.2 installed from the Microsoft Store.
The reporter observes the issue during ordinary browsing and video use, and reports seeing it on multiple systems.
The reporter supplied a PowerToys diagnostic archive after reopening PowerToys, not while the failure state was still present.
The reporter later installed the newest stable release from GitHub and reports that the same behavior recurred.
No software installation was reported during the period leading to the latest observed exit.
There are no assignees on the issue; labels are Issue-Bug, Needs-Triage, Needs-Team-Response, and Product-General.
PR #50273 is a merged, publicly linked diagnostic change for the Runner session-end message path.
inferences: The surviving Command Palette makes a Runner-specific termination path more plausible than a complete PowerToys process shutdown, but this is not confirmed.

Because the archive was created after restart, it may have missed the log and Windows error state needed to distinguish a Runner crash, session-end request, Restart Manager request, or external termination.
The similar reports support prioritizing shared Runner diagnostics, but do not prove that all reports have the same cause.
issue_context.analysis: Current public evidence is sufficient to establish a recurring Runner-facing symptom on a current release, but not to select a safe behavioral fix. The existing maintainer PR instruments the exact tray-window session-end path that could explain a silent Runner exit. The next useful evidence is therefore a fresh failure-time report and Windows error record that can confirm or rule out that path, rather than a speculative watchdog or restart change.
initial_investigation: The current Runner tray-window procedure in src/runner/tray_icon.cpp delegates WM_QUERYENDSESSION and WM_ENDSESSION to handle_stateless_session_end_message.

src/common/utils/window.h shows that a confirmed WM_ENDSESSION destroys the tray window and allows the Runner message loop to exit; ENDSESSION_CLOSEAPP is treated as an application-only close request.
Runner history includes PR #48363, which added the session-end handling to avoid APPLICATION_HANG_QUIESCE during shutdown, sign-out, or restart.
PR #50273 modifies src/runner/tray_icon.cpp to log the session-end message phase and decoded close-app, critical, and logoff flags before that handler executes.
The issue's own public discussion links #50270, #49438, and #49208; all remain open Issue-Bug reports and do not provide a confirmed duplicate or completed remediation.

information_gaps.information: A fresh PowerToys diagnostic ZIP collected immediately after the tray icon and PowerToys tools disappear, before manually restarting PowerToys.
information_gaps.why_needed: It can preserve the Runner state and new session-end diagnostics needed to distinguish the proposed session-end path from a crash or external termination.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: After reproducing on the newest stable release, comment /bugreport immediately after noticing the disappearance and before relaunching PowerToys.

information_gaps.information: The exact installed PowerToys version and install channel, plus any Event Viewer Application Error entry at the observed exit time.
information_gaps.why_needed: It confirms the current build under test and identifies whether Windows recorded a crashing process or termination signature.
information_gaps.how_to_collect: Include the version and install channel in the issue reply, then copy the Event Viewer Application Error details whose timestamp matches the disappearance.

comment.body:
Thanks for confirming that this still happens on the latest stable release and that the earlier archive was collected after restarting PowerToys. PR #50273 has now added Runner logging for Windows session-end and Restart Manager close-app messages. After a preview containing that change is available, please provide:

1. A fresh diagnostic archive by commenting `/bugreport` immediately after the next unexpected exit and before restarting PowerToys if possible.
2. The exact preview version used.

The new archive will distinguish a Windows-requested Runner shutdown from a crash or another termination path.
